title: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: War In Heaven And In Earth

sense.text:
Our lives are at serious risk as we fight the spiritual fight for righteousness. All of us, not just the Bishops, the deacons and the captains, but any of us that seek to do the righteousness of the Lord in a wicked society: our lives are at risk. Christ said “Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness”, and that’s what our job is.

This society don’t want us to hunger and thirst for righteousness. The setup wants to blur the lines between righteousness and wickedness so that you don’t know which is which, and most of our people now are hungering and thirsting for filth, for sin and for lasciviousness. Our eyes have been obscured to follow after wickedness and evil. But for those of us that follow after God’s righteousness, that’s where the blessing is going to come.

The righteousness is the keeping of God’s commandments. You got to know what God’s righteousness is, and that’s why it is read out of the Old Testament and the New Testament both.

“For they shall be filled”: the Most High is going to bless the Israelites that keep his commandments. We’re going to be filled with the glory and the kingdom that the Lord is going to give us.

precepts.why:
Here is what the righteousness is: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God”. That’s the righteousness we’re supposed to hunger and thirst for: God’s righteousness, meaning keeping the commandments, as God has commanded us.

The commandments and the righteousness are synonymous. When you talk about God’s commandments you’re talking about his righteousness. That’s why this scripture was wanted: it correlates perfectly with Matthew, and with Romans.

To attain righteousness in this setup is difficult for many of our people, and mainly the ones in church. The people in the churches are the most deceived, because they have purposely been given a program to deceive them. You’re better off not even going to church; you’re better off in the streets than going into the church, because they purposely frame your mind around wickedness with a covering, making you think it’s about Jesus.

“For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.” The people have a zeal of God; that’s what they go to church for, thinking they’re going to get the Lord in there. “For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness”: ignorant of what we just read in Deuteronomy. The people in the church have no idea what’s required of them. The Lord said, what is it that I require of thee O Israel, and that’s to keep the commandments of the Lord; in the New Testament Christ said the same thing, if you love me keep my commandments.

The objective of the church is to destroy you, straight up. Plain language, no sugarcoating: these churches are basically crack houses with a dope needle to your head, to poison the way you think.

“And going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.” Being ignorant of God’s commandments, they make up their own commandments. That’s going about to establish their own righteousness, which is not righteousness at all; it’s wickedness. The churches say it’s okay, knowing it’s totally different from what the Bible says, and encourage them to go head on with their feelings. Your feelings are going to get you killed. They never found the truth; they never found out what the scriptures mean. They have not submitted to the ways of the Lord, the churches love to have it so, and the people are going to be destroyed if they don’t get out of there.

Christ said it in the New Testament, plain and simple: “keep my commandments.” If you love me, keep my commandments. See how simple that is. Go back to the Old Testament, Deuteronomy 6:25, and it’s the same thing: it shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments. Christ’s commandments and the righteousness we hunger and thirst after are one.

sense.text:
“Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake”. In this wicked society the churches ain’t dealing with the righteousness at all, because they’re not persecuted at all. The persecution comes upon those who are really following God’s commandments. That’s what suffering as a Christian, and not as a murderer, is talking about.

We are persecuted, but we’re persecuted because we’re doing the will of God: keeping the commandments of God, and teaching our brothers and sisters, wives, husbands, men, women and children to do the righteousness that God has recorded in the Bible. That goes against the grain and against the flow of wickedness in this society. We are in the evil days, and for us to live righteously in this we are definitely going to run up against some persecution.

“For theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” Those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake are the ones that’s going to get the kingdom of heaven. See how beautiful that is: we got a kingdom coming. The only thing we need to do is stay steadfast with him, stay on course. Don’t get deterred, don’t get discouraged, don’t get faint-hearted. Stay right here.

War in heaven and in earth. “And ye shall know the truth”: you Israelites shall know the truth, the righteousness of God, “and the truth shall make you free.” That’s a deep statement, because that’s exactly what it does. Like our Elder used to say back in the days, when you know this Bible, you know the future. They showed Moses the beginning, the midst and the ending of time, and we’re sitting in the same seat: we can go inside this Bible and pinpoint all time periods, knowing that the kingdom is coming to us.

That’s a level of freedom for our people who are downtrodden mentally or spiritually, who feel like they have no hope. Then they find out that they’re the Israelites and Christ died for them, and that gives them hope, vision and purpose. All their lives they were told they were nothing and wouldn’t amount to anything, and then they find out that they are in fact the Israelites the Bible speaks of, and that the only thing they need to do is keep Christ’s commandments and the kingdom is theirs. That’s the freedom we’re going to get, and it will help you endure persecution for righteousness’ sake, because we know there’s a reward for what we’re doing.

In this system the truth is considered hatred by those who advocate and teach lies. The truth is called a hate group, evil, repugnant, disdained, unwanted, unfashionable, out of style: ‘oh that’s that old stuff.’ The objective of a liar is to gather and control all minds to conform to the lies, and that’s what the churches are created for. Black churches and white churches are totally different: when the white churches gather to themselves, behind closed doors, they’re talking about world dominance, reading this Bible a whole different way about how to stay in power. Any church that is quote unquote integrated is only integrated for you to join them and be put to sleep by them.

How could you set up a church on top of blood and bones? The Native American people used to own this land; you kill them, move them out the way, put them up on reservations on their own land, relegated to the bathroom of their own house, and then you put a church on top of the blood and the bones and tell the slaves you brought over here, come and learn about Jesus. That theology has not changed at all, whatever label they put on it. The real doctrine is slavery, mental slavery: come learn about being a slave.

They control our minds to the point where we say things like, what’s the matter boss, we sick. When Esau gets out of a cab in Midtown Manhattan looking lost, black people will go, oh you lost, can I help. We are trained to seek to their comfort and don’t even realize it. It’s a deep psychological control, unconscious: by the time you realize it’s happening you’re already doing it. You don’t know what the hell you’re doing; you just look at his white skin and your mind is already programmed to seek to his comfort. You might be helping a mass murderer. You have to catch yourself and stop it. We have a sick love for them and at the same time a hatred for our own brothers: black man get out the cab, nobody won’t say nothing.

The purpose of the truth is to free your mind from this kind of thinking, so that you can seek your own salvation. Don’t seek the salvation of the man getting out of a cab. Seek your righteousness.

Malcolm said in 1963 that you have to read the history of slavery to understand this: there was the house negro and the field negro. Our people are taught to shun our history and stay away from it, but in order to know what happened to us you have to go back and look at the damage that was done to us, so you can make the proper decisions ahead of you. The house negro today got a job and a few benefits, bought a house, and you can’t tell him nothing. He’s looking at it like Jesus got me these things: not I got this because of black people, but because of the Jesus white man, and whatever is needed to please him I’m willing to do. That’s psychologically stamped into his mind whether he says it or not. He was more defensive of the white man’s house than the white man himself, because that same white man is his Jesus that gave him his hog pen.

If your slave master got sick, would it be wrong to pray for him to drop dead? You can’t say that in church. The words slave master went over their mind: he’s Jesus to them, and he’s the one that’s got our people’s minds twisted up. That is not advocating violence or setting fire to anybody’s house, and everybody knows that; an enemy will try to twist the words because they hate the message behind it, which is to lift you out of your mental death. They don’t want that resurrection; they want your mind to stay in a servitude posture. Today you still have house negroes and field negroes.

precepts.why:
When we say field negro, it means we are what Romans 12:2 says. We don’t advocate any violence or arson. What we advocate is for us to have our minds properly set up underneath the Most High’s commandments, so that we can do the right things with our bodies. Your head sits on top of your body; it’s supposed to govern your body, not somebody else’s body. We end up looking out for somebody else’s body while our own body is dying. God put your head on top of your body for you to have some sense to control it and do the things that are needful for it.

“And be not conformed to this world”: this is the field negro. “But be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”: the field negro has a new mind state. It’s basically saying that we don’t have a slave master’s mind.

The Bible is saying for us to have all our minds renewed in this truth. Ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free: that’s the renewing of the mind. Not house negroes and field negroes as such, but us having a mind of God, so that we can follow our proper righteousness and know what to properly hunger and thirst for.

sense.text:
To fix a problem you have to know what the cause of the problem is. You have to get into the deep bowels of the issues causing the sick behavior, and oftentimes we’re taught to ignore that. That’s why the generational gaps matter: you won’t even know anything about the footprints you just walked through. You have to talk to your fathers.

“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age”. Inquire means to seek and ask. Summon your fathers, your elders. Talk to those older people that know something, that can tell you which way to walk, because they already walked it. Value older people. Listen to them older men, because they ain’t all fools. People say, that old fool don’t know nothing, but you can’t get to be old being a fool. A lot of young 20 year olds think they know something and they’re dead as hell, pushing up daisies. An older person in his 50s or 60s can tell you how to get past the years of 20 to 30. You’re 25 years old, what the hell do you know? Talk to them older brothers.

“And prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”: your fathers will tell you the footprints. When a son was born, the father’s footprints were already laid from that point to where he is now; the son has to talk to his father to learn them. The way we are today, we don’t do that. We have no connection to our past.

This history needs to be burned in our people’s heads, because if you don’t know where you came from you’ll end up turning right back around and walking into the same place, without even knowing you were already there. That’s the hog pen mentality: going around and around in a circle in the hog pen, never able to think outside of it, not even realizing you’re walking in a circle, knowing nothing about progressing or going forward.

Twenty years after Malcolm made his point about our mental state, in 1983 you basically had the same mentality, and from that point up to now things have gotten worse: black folks with a white mind.

This scripture runs all through the rest of the class, taken piece by piece, because it shows the whole setup of how we are supposed to move. What we need to understand is that this whole system has been designed to keep us as slaves, and that is the war happening in the earth right now: war in heaven and in earth.

“For now shalt thou go forth out of the city”: that city is Babylon the great. “And thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.” In Babylon the great we shall be delivered. Babylon the actual country, the kingdom, never delivered us from the hand of our enemies; we went from Babylon to Persia in captivity. So the Babylon spoken of here is Babylon the great.

“Be in pain”: pain of the mind, looking at the reality that caused us not to evolve as a people. Outside of the small steps of the Civil Rights and things of that nature, we are still in relatively the same predicament we were in 1963 in how we think as a collective. Twenty years after that, 1983, the same mentality, and from there up to now things have gotten worse: black folks with a white mind. In order to fix a problem you have to know its cause; you have to get into the deep bowels of the issues causing the sick behavior, and we are taught to ignore that. You have to pay attention to the rottenness that’s in us. If you don’t talk to your fathers and your elders, every generation has to start from scratch.

The feeling of pain is given to us by God, and there is a benefit to it. When you have pain in your teeth, it tells you something is wrong with the condition of your teeth; ignore it and it gets much worse, and an abscess with poison in the root can even lead to death. Pain is an alarm clock that seeks to get your attention. There is an abscess in our history, an abscess in our growth, and because we ignored the footsteps behind us we end up walking right back into it. The way we think, the exaggerated startle response, post-traumatic slave syndrome, all of it curtails our progress, and if we don’t go back and find out exactly what happened and how, we stay in it.

Painkillers only silence the alarm clock: get high, get drunk, and you wake up in a stupor still with a damn toothache. Christianity does the same thing. It doesn’t deal with the reason we went into the church in the first place; it makes us feel good for the moment, but we come back out and our homes are still broken, our children still out of order, our men still sent to jail in record numbers. Unemployment, drug addiction, mental illness, homelessness and illiteracy are all still there, because the cause is never addressed, so the pain constantly reoccurs. Immediate gratification is a painkiller; addressing the problem is how you alleviate the pain.

It is not enough to say we went into slavery because we broke the Commandments and leave it at that. Keeping the Commandments is a must, but it won’t be seen that way unless we understand the consequences of not keeping them. Tell somebody all day to brush their teeth after every meal and they might not listen; once they get that pain in the mouth they remember, because that’s history. That’s what Deuteronomy the 28th chapter is all about. Pain is pushback: if you know sticking your hand in the fire will burn you, you have enough sense not to go there, but take a painkiller and you won’t feel your arm burning up. In this wicked society full of temptation, without the pain behind breaking the Commandments you will be encouraged to break them.

Pains and judgments are what cause us to acknowledge our misbehavior, the way parents chastise children. A child that is never chastened grows up spoiled, thinking there’s no consequence for anything, and ends up dead; ignore the pain and you end up with nothing but gums. Pain is what motivates our labor. Look back at the atrocities we went through, see how they messed us up, and we have no choice but to say we got to do something about this: restore the decayed state of our people, as they did in the Maccabean period looking at the pain of the nation of Israel being destroyed.

“And labour to bring forth”: labor is work. In the book Black Men: Obsolete, Single, Dangerous, a man tells how his mother bought him a blue plastic airplane with blue wheels and a string to pull it across the floor, while in Dearborn, Michigan, where the movers and shakers of the automobile industry lived and where black women did day work cleaning white folks’ homes, there were no five and dime stores, only craft shops. There white parents bought their sons airplanes in boxes, wooden parts, directions, glue and small engines; the son assembled it over a day or two, took it outside, and it would fly. That is pain and labor, not immediate gratification. Through it the child learned work ethics, discipline, priority, decision making, science and math principles.

The black child bought the plane already assembled and hoped it rolled on the floor like a car or a truck. He was learning to be a consumer who depended on others to build the plane for him, being trained to use his body from the neck down, while the white upper class boy was taught to build things and run things from the neck up. That is how black people are: 1.4 trillion dollars in consumerism, waiting for somebody to bring us a car, a house. Give this man reparations and he won’t do nothing but put rims on the wheels of the plane, because his education won’t go beyond that.

Everybody has 24 hours in a day; discipline is how you use your minutes. Trim the BS, remove frolic and stupidness, slice out the time, and when the hard work is finished you sit back and appreciate the work of your hands. God created the heavens and the earth from what was in his thoughts first, and man was formulated to do the same: before Adam made a chair or a house or a covering for shame, it had to be in his mind, and then he used his hands to bring the elements out of the earth. Faith without works is dead, faith without discipline is dead. People can only see what was in your head once you put hands to it and bring it into existence.

“Now also many nations are gathered against thee”: stress on against thee. “That say, Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion”: let the nation of Israel be defiled with a messed up mind. The many nations are in cahoots, in agreement, in confederation, to make sure we never wake up.

precepts.why:
Kanye made a statement that the Israelites are black and the white man is not a Jew. He told the truth on that, whatever other issues he has, and the minute he said it the enemies went to attack him, because the objective is to fulfill Psalms 83.

“They have taken crafty counsel against thy people”: all of the nations gathered together against us have taken crafty counsel against the people of the Lord. “And consulted”: to consult is to call in experts, consultants. And who are these experts? Witches, preachers, sorcerers, experts in demonology, consulted on how to keep the children of Israel in mental bondage.

“Against thy hidden ones.” The so-called white man runs around calling himself that, but he ain’t hidden at all. The real Israelites are a hidden people. How are we hidden? They put different names on us and covered up the brand name God gave us, which is Israel: Afro-American, Dominican, Puerto Rican, West Indian, Haitian. That’s what the people know us by, so the real us is hidden.

It took crafty counsel to do that. It’s in their schools and their business practices; anybody with enough prominence who says anything about us being the Jews, they move swiftly to quiet it, quell it, shut it down. That is evil from a wicked consultant, a witch, a preacher that goes through the Bible to find a religion to keep our minds in church, destroyed.

Crafty counsel means we have been given an education that is totally inferior, an education that does not make us free but only teaches us how to be check cashers. What you learn in school and college only teaches us as Black and Hispanic people to stay on the hamster wheel, and even with reparations we would only spin it right there, because that’s the extent of our thinking. As Countering the Conspiracy to Destroy Black Boys shows, by the fourth grade a black son enters the fourth grade failure syndrome: he withdraws from academics, draws close to a football, apathy sets in. A boy measured in the 98th percentile in kindergarten, a walking genius, by the fourth grade didn’t like school, and his aspirations for engineering and technical thinking had vanished. The system is purposely geared to kill the aspirations of your sons. Men like that were featured because what they wrote is beneficial to us, though none of them believed in the Most High.

Read to bring about the pain. “I will go and return to my place”: God says he will go, return to his place, “till they acknowledge their offence”, until we acknowledge our offence, and our offence is us breaking the Commandments of God.

“And seek my face”: by him leaving us, the hope is it will cause us to seek his face; in other words, pay attention to the alarm clock. “In their affliction they will seek me early.” Affliction is pain. In our pain, our affliction, we will seek God early, and that is what is going to make us come and keep the Commandments.

You won’t do any kind of labor if you’re not pushed to do it, because labor is work. The man building the plane would love to fly one already built, but he had to decide it was worth putting in the pain and the time. Affliction is the pain, and the pain is what motivates our labor. Look at the pain and do nothing and you go into the garbage, you destroy yourself; but if the pain is on you and you don’t want to keep feeling it, you will do something to get out of it, and that is labor.

Some of us ignore the pain like women during childbirth with epidurals and other things to mask it. God gave that pain to women as a reminder that they are to be obedient to their husbands, a reminder of how they messed up. This should be loved, because the consequence of not doing it is what’s jacking us up.

“Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection”: the Most High said for the women to learn from their husbands in silence, no back talk, no lip, when the man is telling them what to do out of the scriptures. On the job the white man says clean my windows with newspaper, and she’s in there cleaning it though it ain’t even in her job description, but when her husband asks her something she’s got a problem.

“But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence”: she is not supposed to be over the man, and God set that up. “For Adam was first formed, then Eve”: Adam was made first, Eve came from Adam, and everybody else came from Eve.

“And Adam was not deceived”, because Adam was already a god, a power in the earth; God made him lord over the earth and all his creatures. “But the woman being deceived was in the transgression”: she was deceived by Satan into wanting to be above Adam, in the transgression of listening to Satan to go against her husband. That’s why the Lord said she must learn in silence.

“Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety”: if she follows what the Most High said she will be saved. If she’s running her mouth trying to be over her man she’s not going to be saved, simple as that. A lot of women with that big mouth driving their husbands crazy think they’re going to get the kingdom; they’re going to get death.

Still dealing with the pain, the value and the gift of pain. “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children”: screaming and hollering, pain, pain, pain. It wasn’t supposed to be like this. Every time she has a baby it is a constant reminder of her disobedience against her husband. But he goes to the medical field for painkillers and epidurals so she doesn’t feel it, and she never understands the value of why God gave the pain, which lets her continue to be disobedient to her husband, and that abscess, that toothache, is going to be her death.

“And thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee”: that is what the pain is supposed to remind her of. The Bishop rightly pointed out, and he should know with twelve or fourteen children, that a woman in childbirth is in the most vulnerable position of her whole existence. There ain’t a damn thing she can do if the house catches on fire; she has to be there until it’s finished. God gave that excruciating pain to remind her of the Commandment to obey her husband, and “she shall be saved in childbearing” because in that childbearing she is supposed to remember this.

“And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife”: it was supposed to be him teaching her, but she ended up teaching him, usurping authority over him, and that’s out of order with the Lord. So the Lord gave him pain to remember: “cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life.” “Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee”, “In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground”: work, work, work, when it was given to us in the beginning; until you die. Every time we work it is a reminder that we should not be listening to our wives.

Men need time to think on manly stuff and keep their minds on war, trying to get the kingdom, not carried off into conversations that most of the time ain’t righteous. That doesn’t mean she can’t say nothing; when she comes with scripture, she can speak.

“And Adam called his wife’s name Eve”: he named her, he got his sense back after getting that butt whipping from the Most High. “Because she was the mother of all living”: everybody came from her, Cain and Abel and all the rest of the people.

“Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them”: that is when the law of sacrifice was introduced. The coats of skins are talking about the animals, and the very next chapter proves it.

sense.text: Read to prove that the coats of skins meant the sacrificing of animals. “And Adam knew Eve his wife”: he had sex with her. “And she conceived, and bare Cain”, so Cain was born first.

“And she again bare his brother Abel.” At this time a whole lot of other kids were being born, but only these two are mentioned because they are the subject matter. The Bible is abridged. An exhaustive concordance has every word of the Bible in it; an abridged dictionary has only the keywords, the important words. What we read here is abridged, bringing out the pertinent parts: Adam and Eve had way more children than Cain and Abel, and the chapter proves it when Cain says everyone that finds him will slay him.

“Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.”

“And in process of time it came to pass”: a lot happened in the process of time; kids were being born, people were coming out, and these people lived very long back then. “Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.”

“And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof”: that is the coats of skins, the sacrifice. “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering”, because Abel followed what his father taught him.

“But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect”, because he disobeyed. “And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” This is how the white man is today: the seed of Cain is Esau today, and they think the same exact way.

“Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” He knew what his father taught him, disobeyed, and got mad because he got checked on it. That is exactly how these people are today. Judgment is coming on them and they act like it isn’t supposed to; they have raped, robbed, murdered and pillaged this whole planet and think they’re not supposed to get justice: why is this happening to me?

“If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you had done well like your father taught you, you would have been accepted like your brother. “And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door”: Satan lies at your door, meaning you’re going to be the physical counterpart of the spiritual demon Satan. That’s why they are called the children of the devil.

“And unto thee shall be his desire”: unto Satan shall be the white man’s desire. Just as Eve’s desire was to be to her husband, all her desires met through him, Cain and Cain’s seed get their desires met through Satan. “And thou shalt rule over him”: Satan shall rule over him. That’s all through the scriptures; Revelation says the great dragon gave him his seat and great authority, because Satan is what’s ruling this white man.
“And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.”

“Am I my brother’s keeper?” Listen to the spirit of this dude, knowing damn well he killed him. Knowing damn well this white man killed the Native American Indians: ask where they at and it’s oh, they happily on reservations. No, they dead.
“What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.” The spirit of Abel was crying unto the Father, the same thing we read in Revelation.

“When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength”: this comes all the way up to now. This man has poisoned the earth; where he goes, the earth is poisoned and destroyed. The earth is supposed to be beautiful, but it will not yield its true benefits to this beast. When Israel is back in Jerusalem, back in rulership, the branches shall shoot forth and the earth will yield its strength to us.

“A fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.” Remember that part. He is a fugitive because he committed a crime he has not paid for: he killed his brother Abel, a judgment is supposed to come with that, and he is running from justice. That translates all the way up to Esau.

“My punishment is greater than I can bear. Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid”: he has to hide himself, because everybody is going to be looking to get him. “And it shall come to pass, that every one that findeth me shall slay me.” Who is going to find him, if it’s only his mother and father and he already killed Abel? Those were the other people Eve had.

“Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold.” The Lord blessed Cain with the weapons. Anybody that messes with this dude, vengeance is taken because he’s going to drop bombs on you; he’s got all kind of weapons to obliterate you, and God built him up that way because God is going to ultimately destroy him. Don’t get discouraged by it; these are just the facts.

“And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.” The mark is in his forehead: a mark of technology and weapons, the ability to make weapons. What keeps him from being killed is that he’s got the technology to keep people off of him.

precepts.why:
The spirit is crying out to the Father. “And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God”: Abel was slain for the word of God, because Abel kept the Commandments and brought forth what he was supposed to bring forth and Cain didn’t; that’s why Cain slew Abel. “And for the testimony which they held”: that testimony is to keep the Commandments.

“And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?” That is what the Most High was saying in Genesis: I hear your brother’s voice crying out to me. So it was with the Israelite prophets; a lot of us were killed, and our souls cry to the Most High in the spirit world, and the Lord hears that.

Why vengeance is taken sevenfold on whoever slays Cain: the Lord blessed Cain with the weapons. Obadiah is talking about Esau. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen”: made small among the nations, meaning nothing. “Thou art greatly despised”: despised because he robbed everybody, and all of the nations are trying to get even with him.

So what keeps him? “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”: the pride of his mind deceived him because he has the technology and the weapons to keep people off of him. All of the nations he robbed, and he ain’t got caught yet because he’s got the superior technology, the weapons, the missiles, the guns. You cannot outgun this guy, because God gave that to him as a blessing, as you read in Genesis.

sense.text:
We read that Cain was a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth, with the mark the Lord set on him: the technology and the weapons to keep people off of him. Here is where that changes.

“And it shall be as the chased roe”: the “it” is the white man, the “it” is Esau, and this chapter is talking about Esau. He shall be as a chased deer, because in that day all of the nations are going to be chasing him. “And as a sheep that no man taketh up”: nobody is going to be concerned about him, nobody is going to be trying to protect him in that day; they’re going to be running from him.

“They shall every man turn to his own people, and flee every one into his own land.” Everybody is going to be for themselves in that day; all the nations are going to turn back to themselves.

Why shall he be chased? Because all of the nations that he robbed shall narrowly look upon him and consider him. Isaiah 13 and 14 are talking about the fall of the white man, in plain English: his going down. This is the war in the white man’s heaven. It ain’t the Most High’s heaven at all.

“Every one that is found shall be thrust through”: they’re going to stick a sword through him. “And every one that is joined unto them shall fall by the sword.” Whoever holds on to him as his master is going to die with him. That’s going to be the day to get the hell away from him, the day you got to leave them alone and let the judgment of God come upon them.

“Their children also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes”. This is a terrible thing, man. Those children are the seed of Esau, and in that day they’re going to die. That can’t be dressed up; that’s exactly what we’re reading.

“Their houses shall be spoiled, and their wives ravished”: their wives are going to be raped, and it’s the nations that are going to do that, not the Israelites. That’s a fantasy of some sick Negroes that want a white woman so bad. Israel ain’t going to be doing that at all; rape is against the Bible.

precepts.why:
This is why he shall be chased: “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man”. Is this the big bad white man? Is this the one that we call Jesus, the one that got his churches where all our generations and our black brothers and sisters were going in there?

We see Esau every day, but we see him through a lens that they gave us: a lens to look at them as if they’re great people, as if they’re Superman, the hunks and the beauties, The Bachelor and all that foolishness. To narrowly look means we remove those false glasses. We strain our eyes and take a good look and examine what he really is.

“Is this the man that made the earth to tremble”: with his bombs and his weapons and his technology. “That did shake kingdoms”: he shook kingdoms with bombs. When he walked into the lands and stepped on the soil, everybody bowed, everybody moved out of the way, everybody was scared and shook when this man showed up. In that day it’s not going to be like that.

“That made the world as a wilderness”: with bombs. He poisoned the water, destroyed the ozone layer, destroyed people’s minds. Fish coming up because they can’t take the water no more, birds dropping dead from pollution. This is the man that did this, and that’s why the earth is not going to yield her strength unto this beast. “And destroyed the cities thereof”: who else is this talking about? Esau, the white man.

“That opened not the house of his prisoners”: his prisoners are the twelve tribes of Israel, and everybody else he put in captivity. This is Esau.

This is the reason why he’s going to get it, the law on why they’re going to be chasing him: “Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed”.

Did Esau shed the blood of the nations? Yes. Esau has slain all of the nations. Every nation felt the wrath of Esau; every nation has suffered multiples of loss, multiples of destruction, multiples of captivities and robbery. But what he did to the twelve tribes of Israel is a hundred percent worse. All the rest of the nations got their nationality; they won’t even allow us to say ours. We can’t even say that we’re the Jews. He’s got to pay for all of that.

sense.text:
This proves that Babylon is America. “The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see.” The burden is the trouble, the ugly sight to the Most High: Babylon is a burden.

Isaiah was in the Babylonian captivity at that time, in ancient Babylon. So why does the Bible say he saw Babylon? It would not make sense to say he saw the same Babylon everybody else was in. The Babylon Isaiah was seeing was not the one where he was; he saw the Babylon that everybody else didn’t see. He saw Babylon the great in the vision, and that’s what he’s prophesying about.

“Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain”: that’s what we ought to do in this kingdom, bringing it all the way up to where we are now. “Exalt the voice unto them”: that’s what we’re doing when we teach on the street. “Shake the hand”, with that vehement shaking, making them upset that we’re telling them the black man, the Hispanics and the Native American Indians are the Israelites the Bible speaks of. Now they’re talking in their top courts and all of that, trying to stop this truth. “That they may go into the gates of the nobles”: this truth is going all the way up into the society.

“I have commanded my sanctified ones”: the sanctified ones are the Israelites that repented. That’s us. Sanctified means cleaned up, and what sanctified us is the word of God, the commandments. The sanctified ones are the prophets, the brothers teaching this truth.

“I have also called my mighty ones for mine anger”: when the prophets speak, he sends the angels. The angels are activated by the words of the prophet; the mighty ones back up the sanctified ones. The angels work on the minds of the men and the women, on the minds of kings, on Biden, on Putin. When we speak about war, God is sending the angels to make them make decisions, to press buttons and get the war going. That’s how God’s prophecies come to pass: the prophets speak, the angels are activated, and they go to work on the minds of men to make sure the prophecies in this Bible come to pass. That’s the power that we have.

“Even them that rejoice in my highness”: the angels rejoice in God’s highness.

“The noise of a multitude in the mountains”: the mountains are the governments. The nations are arguing about the Israelites waking up, arguing about the twelve tribes of Israel gathering themselves together. “Like as of a great people; a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together”: like we read in Psalms 83, there’s a whole lot of nations that want to keep the Israelites in slavery.

“The Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle.” Who’s doing this? The Most High. The Lord of hosts is starting the fight; God is causing this.

Now the weapons and the missiles. “They come from a far country, from the end of heaven”: he’s going to send terrorists over here, all kinds of plagues right here. “Even the Lord, and the weapons of his indignation”: the weapons of God’s indignation are those nuclear intercontinental ballistic missiles that he calls the nations to build.

“To destroy the whole land”. Is there an s on that? No. Land is singular: a hundred percent of this country is going to go up in smoke. That’s the Babylon Isaiah was talking about. He was not talking about ancient Babylon; the ancient kingdom of Babylon didn’t get none of this.

“Howl ye; for the day of the Lord is at hand”. The day of the Lord was not at hand in ancient Babylon. The day of the Lord is close now, in this Babylon the great. “It shall come as a destruction from the Almighty”: the day of the Lord shall come as a destruction from God, and it’s going to happen in this Babylon the great.

precepts.why:
“Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.” What sanctified us is the word of God, which is the commandments. That’s what cleaned us up.

When you hear people talking about they’re sanctified, Holy Rollers, that’s bull jive. Sanctification is when you clean up with God’s commandments. That’s who the sanctified ones of Isaiah 13:3 are: the Israelites that repented, the prophets teaching this word.

“Shall a trumpet be blown in the city”: that’s the prophets’ teaching, the alarm. The Jews are black, the Israelites are black, Christ is black, the Lord is coming back to save the nation of Israel: that’s the trumpet being blown, and when the nations hear it they are afraid. “And the people not be afraid?” There’s fear coming out when we speak this word.

“Shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” Our words are bringing evil to this wicked society, because the angels are going to bring the evils. The Book of Psalms tells of the Lord sending evil angels among them.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” Unless the Lord gives his prophets the secrets, the Most High’s angels ain’t going to do anything. His secrets are the prophecies, the prophecies you hear the brothers bringing out, like Deacon Malachi and Bishop Nathanyel, and when those prophecies go out the angels are activated.

Your church members ain’t going to get this; your preachers in church ain’t going to get this. It’s only going to come from the Israelite prophets, which are the sanctified ones. When they teach, the angels move according to the words the prophets speak. That’s the reason why they’re angry with us: they know that when we speak, the angels move.

sense.text:
This proves that the Babylon Isaiah prophesied against was Babylon the great, where we are now, and not the Babylon he was in; that was a vision the Lord gave him.

“And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms”: she is the glory of kingdoms because she robbed everybody else, with her weapons and with her protection. God gave them that mark, the mark of Cain, to protect them and keep the nations from getting him. “The beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency”: what made them beautiful is robbery. She’s decked out with precious pearls and diamonds, like we read in Revelation. Their excellency is their missiles, their weapons, all their riches, their space program, and all of that is going to be burned up.

“Shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” How did God overthrow Sodom and Gomorrah? By fire. That’s how Babylon is going to be destroyed, and we’re in Babylon the great right now. It’s not in Iraq.

“It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation”: that’s the point right there. When the bombs hit this place, it is never going to be inhabited again, because it’s going to be all burnt up with smoke and fire. That’s how he destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, and that’s how he’s going to do this place. That is not Iraq. Isaiah was basically standing in Iraq, where ancient Babylon was, and Iraq is inhabited right now.

“Neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall the shepherds make their fold there.” Some people tried to say that Babylon was over there; the scriptures prove that it ain’t.

“But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of doleful creatures; and owls shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there”. In other words, no human life is going to be here; only little owls, basically buzzards. Like the day after, if anybody ever saw that movie: that’s how this place is going to be. No life is going to be able to live here at all.

precepts.why:
How did God overthrow Sodom and Gomorrah? “Then the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven”. Brimstone and fire is what burnt up Sodom and Gomorrah.

That’s how the Lord is going to destroy this Babylon the great: he’s going to bring brimstone and fire to burn up this place. And where is that fire going to come from? Nuclear weapons.

Revelation reads the exact same thing, and it’s not talking about ancient Babylon. “And after these things I saw another angel come down from heaven, having great power; and the earth was lightened with his glory”: the glory of the Most High. “And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen”. What we read in Isaiah was about Babylon the great. That’s where we’re at, where the children of Israel have been laying dead, like Revelation 11 says, in the street of the great city ‘which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt’.

“And is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit”: that’s what this place is, foul spirits and demonic mess all over here, Christianity and all that. “And a cage of every unclean and hateful bird”: that’s what the 21st verse of Isaiah 13 is talking about, “wild beasts of the desert”, “doleful creatures”, “owls”, basically buzzards. Isaiah was prophesying in connection with what John was writing. That’s what will be left here: a wasteland. That’s why Isaiah 13 said “to destroy the whole land”.

“For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication, and the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth are waxed rich through the abundance of her delicacies.” That’s what made her the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency in Isaiah: she took everybody else’s riches.

“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins”. That means come out of the mindset. We’ve got to be in pain and labor to get out of that slave mindset, because if we don’t, we’re going to die here. When the Lord sets this place on fire, if your mind ain’t right you’re going to die here with your enemies. Our brothers and sisters better repent and get their minds right, because the Lord is not playing.

sense.text: This shows clearly that it’s talking about the white man. “Come near, ye nations, to hear; and hearken, ye people: let the earth hear”: the Most High wants us to hear something.

“For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations”: that’s why Obadiah says the day of the Lord is upon the nations. “And his fury upon all their armies”: whose armies? Mainly the white man’s armies. The Negro ain’t got no army.

“He hath utterly destroyed them, he hath delivered them to the slaughter.” This is past tense. He’s showing you the aftermath: Isaiah is seeing Babylon the great already destroyed, and he’s writing down what he has already seen happen.

“Their slain also shall be cast out, and their stink shall come up out of their carcases”. Can you imagine what this place is going to be like, with a bunch of dead bodies burnt up? Nobody is going to be able to live here. “And the mountains shall be melted with their blood.” Lord have mercy.

“And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved”: this is the heaven part. It ain’t talking about God’s heavens. It’s talking about the white man’s heaven, his kingdoms; the book of Peter explains it.

“And the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: look at a mushroom cloud. That’s what Isaiah saw. Their kingdoms are going to be rolled up like that when a bomb hits, rolled up like a scroll.

“And all their host shall fall down”: all their armies, their navies, all of their weapons are going to be destroyed in that day, when Christ comes back. “As the leaf falleth off from the vine”: that’s how easy it is going to be for the Lord to destroy this whole system, as easy as a leaf falling off of a tree. That’s the kind of power Christ is coming with. He’s not coming back as a man, he’s coming back with full power, and even those that pierced him are going to see him, shaking with terrible fear. In one hour this is all going to be gone: one hour we’re here enslaved, the next hour it’s all gone. That’s how quick the Lord is going to get rid of it. “And as a falling fig from the fig tree.”

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”: not the Most High’s heaven. The scriptures tell you he cometh with a sharp sword, and with it he shall smite the nations, and he’s bathing his sword in the white man’s heaven, him particularly, because he’s got the weapons.

“Behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”: the sword of God shall come down upon Idumea. Idumea is the so-called white man. It’s the Greek word for the name Edom, particularly the so-called Jews, and it comes down on all the so-called white man. Put up on the board, Idumea means of or relating to Edom.

The Pictorial History of Jewish Civilization, a very prestigious book, proves that Edom is the white man and that God’s sword is against him. It was a gift passed between white people, best wishes on this special day, passing these books backwards and forwards to each other while the poor little Negro doesn’t know what the hell is going on. The Negro was never supposed to get his hands on it. We bought it at a bookstore in New York where the scholars sent their used books. We didn’t spend our money on no damn rims and sneakers; we bought books.

Inside, the book shows painted clay plaques from a building erected by Ramses II, the king that was in charge when the Israelites were in bondage: the thousands of war captives, transformed into slaves, that made it possible for the Egyptian kings to implement their feats of engineering. Chained captives. Look at the facial features on those people, the brown color on the face, the yoke of iron around the neck. That woman is not a white woman. This is not a comic book; these are thousands of years old, from the walls of Ramses’ time, a building that we built. Those lying bastards, the so-called white people, know us from a building erected by Ramses II; that’s our people that were in Egyptian bondage. We need to have this history burned in our brain.

On page 94 they write: Lord of the universe, is it not enough for your sons what the evil kingdom of Edom Rome did to them? Edom Rome: that’s the whole white world, the Greco-Roman Empire, the so-called white man. And they write that there will be a great hatred between them and the children of Esau Rome. The children of Esau Rome are the Idumeans. They know it is them. My sword shall be bathed in Idumea, which is Babylon the great, right here.

“And upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” What is the people of God’s curse? Esau. The curse is not only the leprosy, but mainly that they’re going to be destroyed: the curse the Lord put on these people is that they are the vessels of God’s wrath. That’s why he created them. They have no other purpose but to fight against God, so that God can exercise his power in destroying them. The Most High is going to bring that destruction through them.

“The sword of the Lord is filled with blood”: filled with the white man’s blood, in his heavens. “It is made fat with fatness”: there’s going to be a lot of blood on that sword. “With the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams: for the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah”. Check the history: Bozrah was the capital of Edom. “And a great slaughter in the land of Idumea”: the land of Idumea is America.

precepts.why:
This shows what the curse is. Esau is in verse 22, Jacob is in verse 23. “What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known”: God is going to show his power off. “Endured with much longsuffering”: he endured, watching this white man run around calling himself a Jew and disregarding the real Jews. God knows this man is a liar, but God made him that way.

“The vessels of wrath”: a vessel is something you channel liquid through. The Most High is going to channel his anger through the vessel of the white people. “Fitted to destruction”: he was made to be destroyed. That’s his purpose; that’s the curse God gave him. I’m going to show my power by destroying you.

That’s the same as Pharaoh: God raised up Pharaoh so he could show his power through him, and he says the same thing to Esau: ‘for the same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might show my power in you’, when I destroy you.

“And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy”: that’s Jacob, the Israelites. We are the vessels of God’s mercy; Esau is the vessel of God’s wrath. That is the people of God’s curse in Isaiah 34:5, the ones the sword comes down upon.

sense.text:
“And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon”. The dragon is the so-called white man: the great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns. The seven heads are Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Britain. All of those are white people. “And the dragon fought and his angels”.

Out of the seventh head came an eighth head, recorded in the 17th chapter. That eighth head is America, and it shall go into perdition, which means destruction.

precepts.why:
“And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT”. Mystery is the first name: people don’t know where Babylon the great is. They’re acting like they don’t know. They think it’s in Iraq, they think it’s here, it’s there. It’s a mystery because they’re trying to figure out where it is, and it’s here. Babylon is great confusion: man don’t even know if he’s a man or not.

“THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS”: America sleeps with every nation in their politics and makes them all get in bed with her with their democracy. “AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH”: homosexuals, lesbians, all abominations. This is the land of abominations right here.

“And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus”: that’s the prophets. They’re going to kill a lot of us. A lot of people got killed in this country, and they ain’t done yet, but the Most High said he’s got us. We ain’t worrying about it.

“When I saw her, I wondered with great admiration. And the angel said unto me, Wherefore didst thou marvel?” John is seeing all of this go down, and he needs explanation. “I will tell thee the mystery of the woman, and of the beast that carrieth her, which hath the seven heads and ten horns.” The seven heads are named above; the ten horns are ten common markets.

“The beast that thou sawest was, and is not”: it was in John’s vision, but it was not in existence at the time John was writing. America did not exist. “And shall ascend out of the bottomless pit”: the bottomless pit is Europe; it came out of Britain. “And go into perdition”: when it comes, it shall go into destruction. That’s where we’re at now; the bombs are going to hit it.

“Whose names were not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world”: America is not written in the Bible, because America as a physical place did not exist. It existed in spirit, and that’s why John was able to write about it. “When they behold the beast that was, and is not, and yet is”: it was in his vision, it was not in existence yet, and yet it is coming.

“And here is the mind which hath wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman sitteth.” The seven heads are seven governments: Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Britain. “And there are seven kings”: it’s crystal clear. These are red kings, the so-called white man. He’s not white, he never has been white, he’s always been red; that’s why it’s called the red dragon.

“Five are fallen, and one is”: the one that is, is Rome, the one John was in. “And the other is not yet come”: that’s Britain. “And when he cometh, he must continue a short space”, because America broke off from Britain.

“And the beast that was, and is not, even he is the eighth, and is of the seven”: America came out of Britain, which came out of the other heads. “And goeth into perdition”: goeth into destruction, the bombs. My sword shall be bathed in heaven. That’s why we’re waking up now: we’re in that time.

sense.text:
This proves the war in heaven is talking about nuclear destruction. “For every battle of the warrior is with confused noise”: these are the wars fought on this planet before the nuclear wars we have now. The fighting in the trenches, with swords, bayonets in the lungs, heads chopped off, arms chopped off: confused noise, people screaming, I’m dying. “And garments rolled in blood”: when they got stabbed with the bayonets, legs missing, the bloody garments wrapped around them as they were carried on the gurneys.

“But this shall be with burning and fuel of fire.” The war that’s coming after that is going to be with burning and fuel of fire. That’s nuclear missiles. And whose words is Isaiah bringing? The Most High’s.

precepts.why:
“Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire”: God created the blacksmith, a man that makes weapons. The blacksmith blew the coals to make the fire big so he could bend steel to make shields, bucklers, swords, helmets: weapons for war.

“And that bringeth forth an instrument for his work”: God calls the smith to bring forth an instrument for war, for God’s work. “And I have created the waster to destroy”: to destroy the whole land, like we read in Isaiah 13.

The waster is a nuclear bomb. The prophets didn’t even really know what to call it. They saw it in their mind and didn’t know how else to describe it. It’s a waster, because when it hits, everything is gone.

This is Malachi trying to describe his part of this destruction: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”. What day has there ever been on this earth where it felt like you were in an oven on full blast? What kind of weapon back then produced anything like that? Nothing. That is the “burning and fuel of fire” of Isaiah 9:5; that’s what Malachi was being shown: war in heaven.

“And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up”: the day that feels like an oven is going to burn the people up. “That it shall leave them neither root nor branch”: the trees, everything, is going to get burnt up.

Revelation 7 speaks of it: the angels were holding back the wind, that it should not blow on any tree, until the servants of God were sealed in their foreheads, until the twelve tribes of Israel returned to the Most High. Regular wind blows every day; that was the wind of destruction, what we read here, the day that feels like an oven. There are so many scriptures in the Bible that clearly point to this.

“And this shall be the plague wherewith the Lord will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem”: that’s the so-called Jews, that’s the so-called Negroes, that’s everybody that was fighting this gospel, every one that turned their back on this gospel, the turncoats, all of them that tried to destroy it. They’re going to pay too. If you are found fighting against this truth, this is going to be your fate.

Add up what we’ve been reading. This war shall be with burning and fuel of fire. Another prophet says it shall be a day that burns as an oven. Another says it is a waster. Another scripture says it shall destroy the whole land, land singular, with the weapons of God’s indignation. Now we’re reading the effects of the heat.

“Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet”. What can make your flesh evaporate from your bones before your body has a chance to react to gravity and pull your skeleton to the ground? By the time your skeleton hits the ground, all the flesh off your bones is going to be evaporated because of that heat.

“And their eyes shall consume away in their holes”: their eyes are going to melt in their sockets. That’s twofold: your eyes will literally melt in your sockets, and your vision of going beyond what the Most High said is going to end. You ain’t going to be telling yourself what you’re going to be doing after that; you’re going to be dead.

“And their tongue shall consume away in their mouth”: all that talking philosophy about what Esau is going to continue to do, that’s going to be closed in that day, and the tongue is literally going to melt in his mouth, because the heat is going to burn it up. This is crystal clear.
